title: How to Read Any Sign: Shapes & Colours
whatItIs: UK road signs follow a simple system: the shape tells you what job the sign does, and the colour tells you more about it.
keyFacts: Circles give orders, triangles warn and rectangles mostly give information.
Red circles mostly tell you what you must not do; blue circles mostly tell you what you must do.
STOP (octagon) and GIVE WAY (upside-down triangle) have their own shapes so they stand out.
Direction signs are colour-coded: blue for motorways, green for primary routes, white for other roads.
A plate below a sign adds to or limits its message, for example times or distances.

visual.caption: Read the shape first, then the colour

items.title: Circle = order
items.text: Tells you what you must or must not do.

items.title: Triangle = warning
items.text: Tells you about a hazard ahead.

items.title: Red ring = prohibition
items.text: Mostly tells you what you must not do.

items.title: Blue circle = positive order
items.text: Mostly tells you what you must do, like 'turn left'.

items.title: STOP and GIVE WAY
items.text: Unique shapes so you recognise them at once.

a.label: Blue circle
points: An order: you must do it
For example: ahead only, turn left

b.label: Blue rectangle
points: For example: one-way traffic, motorway signs

onTheTest.question: What does a circular sign with a red border usually tell you?
onTheTest.why: Red rings mostly prohibit. Blue circles give positive orders, triangles warn and rectangles inform.

traps: A blue rectangle is information; a blue circle is an order.
The upside-down triangle is GIVE WAY: an order, not a warning.
Plates under a sign change or limit what it means, such as times or distances.
